newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bosnia peace stabilisation plan adopted.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia peace stabilisation plan adopted.

text.p: Bosnia's three co-presidents and major world powers approved a two-year stabilisation plan to bolster fragile peace in the former Yugoslav republic at a conference in Paris on Thursday.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette announced that a 13-point plan pledging international aid in return for the completion of Bosnia's joint institutions and a series of other pledges on refugees, freedom of movement and human rights was adopted at a three-hour ministerial meeting in Paris.

Without specifically committing the international community to keep a military presence in Bosnia when the mandate of the current Peace Implementation Force (IFOR) expires next month, the document said:

"Recognising the fundamental importance of a secure environment to the task of civilian implementation, the participants welcomed the ongoing study by NATO members in cooperation with other states participating in IFOR of options dealing with the evolving situation."

International mediator Carl Bildt, whose powers were increased by the agreement, adopted 11 months after the Dayton peace accord was signed in Paris, said a successor force must stay in Bosnia during the entire two-year consolidation period.

However, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said Bonn wanted it limited to one year. It would be wrong to give the rival Bosnian factions the impression that international aid could be dragged out over several years, he said.
